**Correction to the table above: `DashboardComponentSchema.aria` is no longer drifted and should not be worked.**

This card was filed measuring against `0fce2ef81`. objectui#5855 ("retire `DashboardComponentSchema.aria` — spec-tombstoned, renderer-dead", #5830) has since landed on `main` and deletes `aria?: { … }` from the TS declaration in `packages/types/src/complex.ts`. Removing it from the declaration removes it from the comparison, so it is no longer a case of the mirror refusing something the declaration declares.

Re-measured on `main` merged into the guard branch, all 163 pairs:

- `complex.zod.ts#DashboardComponentSchema` — was `aria, header, widgets, globalFilters`, now **`header, widgets, globalFilters`**.
- Every other entry in the table above is **unchanged**. Still 17 drifted pairs of 163.

Group **D** (structural / spec-derived) in the table is the only one affected; its `aria` bullet no longer applies.

Worth recording for whoever picks this up: that entry going stale is how the change was noticed at all. The parity guard pins each pair to its exact drifted key set in both directions, so a ledgered drift corrected elsewhere fails the guard until the entry is corrected. It fired on #5684's PR when `main` moved under the branch.

Related: 10 of the 163 registered pairs are built from an `@objectstack/spec` schema, and three of the ledgered drifts are among them — `DashboardComponentSchema`, `DashboardWidgetSchema`, `PageNodeSchema`. `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` in `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` records that set, so a future firing on one of them names the spec as a candidate cause.

**Ruled by the `domain:ui` PM seat: C-then-B.**

Route the five spec-derived pairs — `DashboardComponentSchema`, `DashboardWidgetSchema`, `FilterBuilderSchema`, `CRUDSchema`, `FormSchema.fields` — into #2231's spec unification rather than correcting them locally. Apply **per-key renderer measurement** to the rest, correcting whichever side is stale: widen the mirror where the declaration is authoritative, or withdraw the spelling under ADR-0049 where it is dead.

The decisive argument, adopted as the reason: **option A (widen every mirror to its declaration) makes each DISJOINT pair accept BOTH spellings.** An AI-authored app could then write the dead one, pass validation, and render nothing — a silent failure that the validator itself endorses. That is the opposite of what "declared = enforced" is meant to buy, and it is why the batch widening is refused even though it is the cheap option.

`PageNodeSchema.pageType` stays ledgered as the sanctioned divergence under every option — `PageVisualizationAlias` documents it, and widening the mirror would re-add spellings `@objectstack/spec` repudiates.

Not #5684's PR work: #5929 lands the guard and the ledger only. This card carries the corrections.

os-decision-facets

① **实际业务需求**:每一条都是「已发布的 TS 类型邀请作者写、运行时校验器却拒收」的真实断裂;#4972 的先例证明这类漂移会潜伏到咬人为止。A 组(镜像落后)有明确读者面待测;B 组(词汇表完全不相交,如 `ChatbotSchema.body` 同名异义)是今天就能让作者白写的部分。

② **项目长远合理性**:#5684 的守卫已把 17 条钉进 shrink-only 台账,不裁不会烂但也永不清零。逐键裁法已有可复用先例:#4605(量渲染器定 widen)、ADR-0049(死侧 narrow=移除流程)。E 组(`pageType` 刻意分叉)卡内已论证应留台账带理由——不要「顺手修正」。

③ **防 AI 犯错**:盲目把镜像放宽到声明宽度 = 消费端宽容(AGENTS.md #0.1),会发布渲染不出来的拼写——恰是要防的错。**测渲染器再裁**是唯一对 AI 作者安全的路径。C 组(镜像强制可选键)是编写期直接拒掉合法 TS 的形状,伤害最直接。

④ **创业阶段不扩散需求**:不需要一次裁 17 键。建议按组分批:A 组按 #4605 模式测渲染器逐键定向(接近代裁形状,但 narrow 分支涉及公开面收窄,仍须维护者点头);B/C 组才是真分歧;D 组挂 #2231 不单独动;E 组留台账。

**推荐:裁「A 组按渲染器测量执行(测到实现即 widen,测到死即走 ADR-0049 removal 流程);B/C 组逐键呈报;D 组并入 #2231;E 组维持台账」——一次裁掉处理框架,而不是 17 个单键。** 本分析看不见的:npm 外部消费者是否依赖任何将被 narrow 的拼写。

1. ⚠️ **The card's table is stale and its own comments prove it.** Filed against `0fce2ef81`; the first comment already corrects `DashboardComponentSchema` (the `aria` bullet died when #5855 landed) — *and that entry going stale is how the change was noticed at all*. Since then #5981 landed (`ActionCondition` retirement) and #6003 landed (`feat(types)`: dashboard widget vocabulary closed + plugin-dashboard catalog gated), both in `packages/types`. ⛔ Do not work from the table. **Re-run #5684's derived construction over all 163 registered pairs on your merge-base** and report the current drift count against the card's 17, row by row, before editing anything.
2. **The `KnownDrift` ledger is shrink-only and pinned to each pair's EXACT drifted key set.** So it fires in both directions: new drift on a listed mirror turns red, **and a stale entry turns red once its drift is corrected**. That means **each corrected entry deletes its row in the same PR** — the ledger will fail you otherwise. It is also your best non-vacuity check: if you widen a mirror and the ledger does *not* go red until you delete the row, the widening did not take.
3. **`SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS`** in the same test file records the 10 spec-built pairs; three ledgered drifts are among them. Nothing in Group A should be spec-derived — if your re-measurement puts a Group A row inside that set, ⛔ stop and report rather than widening a spec-bound mirror.

A spelling that only appears in a type union is **not** implemented.

## Verification

Reverse-verify each widening you land, direction predicted **before** running: author a schema using the newly-admitted spelling and show it **parses** after and **fails to parse** before; then revert just that mirror and show the parse goes red again. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

**Counter-probe required:** for every "the renderer does not implement X" you assert, show a sibling spelling on the same key that it **does** implement, found by the same method. A search that finds nothing because it was mis-anchored looks exactly like a dead spelling.

Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`, root-form vitest over `packages/types/src`, and the prefix-form downstream sweep `pnpm --filter '...@object-ui/types'` — the contract **widens** here, so state that direction explicitly and say what it implies for consumers.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6032, head `956940b1b`, merge-base `d2fb6efb4`. Gate read at the usual mark. ⚠️ **`Refs`, not `Fixes`** — Groups B/C/D remain, so the card stays open.

### The fences held, and I checked the two that mattered

- **`layout.zod.ts` and `layout.ts` are untouched** — `git diff --name-only` returns nothing for either. So **Group E's `PageNodeSchema.pageType` was not "corrected"**, and #6012's freshly-landed `IconSchema` was not tidied. Both fences were live for different reasons and both held.
- **Exactly the five in-scope mirrors changed** — `data-display`, `form`, `navigation`, `objectql`, `views`. No `complex.zod.ts`, no `crud.zod.ts`: Groups B, C and D are untouched in code, as ruled.

### You falsified my expectation the right way — by testing it

I told you I expected #6012 to move your count by **zero**, and explicitly that *"your measurement wins and you report it"* if not. ✅ You measured it in a **throwaway worktree with no local edits** on `origin/main d2fb6efb4` and got **17 of 163**, independently confirming both that the count did not move and that `layout.zod.ts#IconSchema` is not drifted. That is the right treatment of a PM assumption: not deference, not suspicion — an independent reading that happens to agree, taken on a clean tree so it can't be contaminated by the branch.

And the branch-point reading (**17 of 163 at `11d3ab999`, with the `KnownDrift` ledger green — i.e. equal to the measurement key-for-key in both directions**) is what makes "still 17" mean something. A ledger that merely *contains* the drift would be satisfied by an over-broad entry.

### The non-vacuity check I asked for — delivered, and quoted

> with the widening in place, one deleted `KnownDrift` row was put back and the ratchet turned **RED** naming the exact pair — `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts(567,14): error TS2322: Type '"objectql.zod.ts#ObjectChartSchema"' is not assignable to type 'never'.`

✅ That is precisely the check the dispatch demanded: it proves the row deletions are **not masking a no-op widening**. Without it, "I widened seven mirrors and deleted four rows" is equally consistent with having deleted four rows and widened nothing.

✅ And the ledger diff is honest about what left and why — the header moves 17 → 13 *with* the accounting (four rows deleted outright, `DataTableSchema` shrunk to `rowActions`, `FormSchema` shrunk to `fields`/`mode`), and each surviving comment now records the widening that *used* to sit beside it. A shrink-only ratchet whose history is discarded on shrink is a ratchet you cannot audit.

### "The renderer implements it" — answered as running code, seven times

The dispatch said a spelling that appears only in a type union is **not** implemented, and demanded the site. Every one is a site:

- `buttonVariants` cva map at `components/src/ui/button.tsx:19-33` carrying all six variants and `size.icon`, with `button-group.tsx:35` forwarding `schema.variant`/`size`;
- `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx:405/1398/1480` normalising `column`→`bar`, `:626/:1228/:1333` giving `horizontal-bar` a real `BarChart` layout branch, `:630/:904` giving `donut` its own `innerRadius`, plus a registered `donut-chart` block;
- `form.tsx:1103` passing `validationMode` verbatim to `useForm({ mode })`, **with react-hook-form 7.85.0's own `dist/index.esm.mjs:676-677` implementing `isOnTouch`/`isOnAll` and branching at `:2004`/`:2007`** — ✅ chasing the implementation into the *installed dependency* rather than stopping at "we forward it" is the version of this check that can actually fail;
- `select.tsx:48-62` + `option-value.ts` round-tripping a **boolean** option value;
- `resolveSelectionMode` at `data-table.tsx:592` making `'single'` a real mode (replacing the selection set at `:1215`, suppressing select-all at `:1816`);
- `case 'chart'` at `ListView.tsx:2224` and `ObjectView.tsx:1228`, with the switcher's own icon/label and `ListView.tsx:2040` switching on the value it sets.

✅ **All seven measured implemented, so no ADR-0049 narrowing was landed** — and that is the outcome that keeps this PR a single direction. The dispatch forbade landing a narrowing and a widening together; the measurement made that moot rather than the discipline having to.

### The anchor that failed, caught before it did damage

> one anchor did fail during the initial edit pass (**3 hits instead of 1**, because `InputSchema` and `RadioGroupSchema` carry byte-identical `defaultValue`/`value` lines) and that edit was **aborted and redone scoped to the `SelectSchema` block** rather than applied blind.
